answers.children: Yes — English Foxhounds are good with children thanks to their sociable nature and pack-oriented background that supports living with a group. Their medium build and energetic play style suit older children who can join long walks, while the independent streak means they do not crowd toddlers. The tireless stamina bred for hunting foxes in packs translates to endless games that match active family life. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: English Foxhounds get along well with other dogs because of their pack-hunting history that bred them for harmony in large groups of hounds. Strong prey drive can trigger chasing of smaller pets though, so careful introductions help. Their sociable temperament extends to canine companions yet the independent side may create occasional same-sex tension in intact dogs.
answers.exercise: English Foxhounds need two hours or more of vigorous daily exercise such as long runs or secure off-lead hikes that match their exceptional stamina for hunts. Without this outlet the tireless hunter becomes restless and may chew or pace the house like a caged animal. Scent games suit the breed because its nose was developed to track foxes across countryside terrain.
answers.shedding: Yes — English Foxhounds shed moderately with short smooth coats that leave fine hair on furniture and clothing year-round. The single-layer texture produces less volume than double coats yet still requires weekly brushing to manage loose hairs from their active lifestyle. Their pack-hunting build means the coat stays low-maintenance even after hours in the field.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and English Foxhounds are not among those suggested for allergy sufferers because their short smooth coat still releases dander during shedding. The single-layer hair lacks the dense undercoat that can trap allergens yet it still spreads protein with their energetic movement. Owners must maintain regular cleaning to reduce household levels.
answers.training: English Foxhounds are not easy to train because their independent nature and strong prey drive often override commands during scent work. Bred to hunt foxes in packs without constant direction they show intelligence in tracking yet low biddability when recall conflicts with instinct. Patience and consistent outlets for their melodic voice and stamina improve results over time.
answers.lifespan: English Foxhounds live 10-13 years. Their health robustness supports steady endurance for the long hunts they were developed to perform in English countryside packs. The medium-weight muscular build from 16th-century hound crosses helps them maintain condition when given the vigorous activity their tireless nature demands.
answers.size: English Foxhounds reach 60-75 lb and stand 21-25 in tall as adults. The solid yet athletic build feels substantial when a sociable pack hound leans in for ear scratches after exercise yet remains agile enough for hours of running. Their proportions reflect selective breeding by hunt clubs to balance speed and stamina in group work.
answers.barking: English Foxhounds bark frequently with a melodic baying voice developed to communicate during pack hunts of foxes. They vocalise at scents or movement rather than strangers and their energetic independent streak leads to early-morning choruses if a squirrel passes. The sociable temperament means they bay more when other dogs join in.
answers.apartment: No — English Foxhounds do not suit apartment living because their high energy and melodic voice clash with confined spaces and close neighbours. Bred for endless stamina across open terrain they struggle to settle indoors without two hours of vigorous exercise and become restless. The independent hunter needs secure outdoor access to prevent destructive pacing.
answers.first-time: No — English Foxhounds are not a good first dog because their independent streak and strong prey drive demand experienced handling to channel the tireless stamina bred for pack fox hunts. Novices may be overwhelmed by the need for hours of exercise and management of their baying voice in daily life.
